narrative.overview:
The interface reads like a scoreboard bolted to the wall of a sports hall: technical, flat, square-edged, and glanceable from the next table over. Everything is set in a monospaced face, so names, numbers and pairings line up in columns and nothing competes with the one fact a player needs: where they play and with whom.

Color is nearly absent. Ink on paper carries the interface, and a single blue, taken from the project's existing blue token, is reserved for the table-tennis-table graphic and the actions tied to it. Depth is never shadowed.
keyCharacteristics: Gamified through data (stars, ranks, streaks, progress), never through ornament.
Multilingual by construction: no fixed-width labels, no text baked into graphics.
Monospaced throughout; columns align, numbers scan.
Near-monochrome neutrals plus one blue accent.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, no shadows.
Usable one-handed on a phone at the table.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Table Blue is the only chromatic color on any screen, and it marks the table. If a second hue appears, it is Foul Red for an error, nothing else.

rules.name: The Column Rule
rules.body: Names and numbers that belong together share a monospaced column. Never switch to a proportional face for data.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces carry no shadow at rest or on hover. Hierarchy comes from tone, borders and position.

rules.name: The Square Edge Rule
rules.body: Controls and status labels have no rounding. Rounded shapes are reserved for the table graphic if its design calls for it.

dos: Do use monospaced type for all names, counts and labels.
Do use Table Blue only for the table graphic and its tied actions.
Do separate surfaces with Hairline borders and tone, not shadows.
Do design for a phone held in one hand at the table.
Do express game state with stars, numerals and segmented bars in the system's own style.
Do size labels to content and keep all text translatable.
Do place new elements on the existing 4px step and column structure.
donts: Don't use emoji anywhere in the UI, including as icons or rewards.
Don't use gradients, glows or glassy effects.
Don't use borders thicker than 1px; selection and focus use tone and the 1px ring.
Don't use more than one typeface or mix weights beyond regular and medium.
Don't place elements by one-off margins or arbitrary widths; no fixed-width text boxes.
Don't bake text into images or SVG.
Don't round controls or labels into pills.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; Foul Red is for errors only.
Don't mix a proportional sans into data columns.
